walkthroughs.body_html:
Climate Change & Energy — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Climate Change & Energy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Climate Change & Energy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.
